evidence: The id is a base36 rendering of a sha256 truncated to hashBytesForLength(length), 2 bytes at MinHashLength=3, and TakenFunc only probes the local store, so 'collide only if their whole content and their creation nanosecond match' is false as an absolute. The agent corrected all three copies and rightly declined the reviewer's opposite overclaim that CollisionProbabilityThreshold=0.25 means a 25% collision chance.
guidance_note: When writing a uniqueness guarantee for a truncated hash, state it as a birthday probability against unseen stores from the first draft; never derive id uniqueness from input uniqueness.

evidence: Before ff6a41d only Creator, CreatedAt and nonce were pinned, so dropping c.Title from the format string kept every test green. The agent folded the two existing subtests and the three missing fields into one table over Content mutators, and showed the title row fails when c.Title is removed.
guidance_note: When a doc comment claims every field of a struct feeds a hash, write the test as a table over all of the struct's fields in the same commit as the claim.

evidence: The agent confirmed that the Unreleased Fixed entry still said 'A child id is minted as <parent>.<highest existing child number + 1>' in the present tense next to the new Changed entry. It past-tensed that entry and a second present-tense re-mint claim the reviewer had not named.
guidance_note: When a change supersedes a mechanism, grep the same Unreleased changelog section and the docs for present-tense descriptions of the old mechanism before opening the PR.

evidence: A 3-char base36 suffix is all digits with probability (10/36)^3, about 2.1% per child, so the strconv.Atoi assertion this PR added flaked on a correct minter. ff6a41d deleted the assertion and the strconv import, which is the first remedy the reviewer offered, and left the parentage and distinctness checks.
guidance_note: Before asserting a property of a hash's rendering, such as 'not all digits', compute whether the generator can emit the excluded value; assert the contract (distinct, under the parent) instead.

evidence: The flagged commit ff6a41d touched only tests. The real cause is F1's fix 7861b72, which corrected the 'collide only if ... nanosecond' sentence but left 'No second create lands on the first's nanosecond, so the slot cannot be reoccupied' two lines below it. That sentence rests on the same false reasoning, and the agent admits 'I fixed the sentence the review pointed at rather than the class of claim'. single-enforcer concerns code that enforces an invariant, not repeated prose claims.
guidance_note: When a finding refutes a line of reasoning, grep for every claim that rests on that reasoning (here 'nanosecond' and 'cannot'), not just the quoted sentence and its verbatim copies.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive. ff6a41d did not touch firstIssueID's '.<n>' comment; the comment went stale with the original PR, and the round-0 summary had already reported it at internal/cli/new_test.go:19 under 'Findings outside the reviewed diff', where the agent never acted on it. The fix also caught the same stale shape in the `lit new --parent` help text and in docs/cli-reference.md.
guidance_note: Act on the review summary's 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' list in the same round as the inline threads; when a PR changes an id shape, grep the whole repo for descriptions of the old shape, including help text.

narrative: The PR replaced counter-based child ids with content-hashed ids. Round 0's four findings were all real, and all were fixed well; the F2 table refactor and the F4 assertion deletion were better than the literal suggestions. Round 1 had two findings, both avoidable. F5 is the sibling of F1's overclaim that the first fix did not sweep, and F6 is a stale comment that round 0 had already reported outside the diff and the agent ignored. Round 2 approved, so round 2 exists only because of those two misses.
guidance_observations: The agent swept by class only after the second round; in round 1 it grepped claims and found a fourth copy plus help text, and doing that in round 0 would have prevented round 2.
Out-of-diff findings in the review summary body were dropped in round 0 because they had no inline thread to reply to.

evidence: The hunk shows remoteHeadSchema narrowed to (version, err) while the test kept the name TestRemoteHeadSchemaReadsVersionAndProducer and a doc comment claiming it checks the producer stamp. 6694006 renamed the test and also removed the now-dead producer seed parameter, verified by running the store tests.
guidance_note: When narrowing a function's return values, rename and re-describe every test whose name or doc lists the removed value.

evidence: The cost claim is overstated: the agent measured version.Get() at 1.4-2.9 µs once per process, in commands that open Dolt. The read is already at the boundary, and the guard would duplicate syncPushFailureLines' failed-record predicate. One reviewer point does stand and the agent rebutted it inaccurately: on a version.Get error the 'push-outcome provenance unavailable' stderr line prints even when no failure is recorded, contrary to 'lit really was about to render push-outcome provenance'. That error path signals a genuine registry fault, so leaving the code alone is defensible.
This duplicates F1, the stale test name and doc after remoteHeadSchema dropped the producer return. The same commit, 6694006, fixed it.
guidance_note: When narrowing a function's return values, rename and re-describe every test whose name or doc lists the removed value.

evidence: This duplicates F1 and adds that the producer seed argument is dead weight. 6694006 removed that parameter from seedFutureSchemaRemote and advanceRemoteToFutureSchema and from all five call sites.
guidance_note: When deleting a reader of a fixture field, delete the fixture parameter that only fed it in the same change.

evidence: pushOutcomeProvenance checked only rec.ObservedBy != running but rendered 'so this verdict predates your binary', which is false after a rollback. The agent took the reviewer's direction-neutral option ('so the binary has changed since this verdict') and correctly declined semver comparison, because install.sh stamps git-describe values such as 0.2.1-5-g50dfc53.
guidance_note: Make a rendered sentence claim no more than the predicate guarding it checks; an inequality test supports 'changed', not 'newer'.

evidence: runDoctor does read version.Get() twice, but both reads come from link-time constants and the in-process registry max, so they cannot diverge. Threading version.Info through resolveBuildStatusNote would widen a signature across unrelated callers to save about 2 µs. The reviewer's 'fan-out' reading of version.Get's cache advice misapplies it to one call per process.

The .goreleaser.yml ldflags comment states 'lit version therefore reports lit 0.1.0, not lit v0.1.0', and the agent also cites install.sh's ver="${ver#v}", so the doc and changelog examples showed output the binary cannot produce. 6694006 changed the docs, the changelog and the test fixtures to bare versions.
guidance_note: When documenting rendered output, copy the example from the actual producer's convention (the goreleaser and install.sh stamps), not from an invented fixture value.

evidence: The finding exists because post-review commit 6963040 trimmed the comments carrying [LAW:polishing-by-subtraction], visible in sync_failure.go and sync_schema_guard.go. That commit was a comment-trim answering no finding, so no earlier finding id applies and caused_by is null. On the merits, Canonical is documented as 'transcribed verbatim from the universal-laws Token index', so membership follows the index rather than current citations. The packet does not show the index itself; the agent asserts the token is in it.

narrative: Round 0 raised seven findings: three duplicates of one stale test name, a real false-direction claim in the provenance clause, a v-prefix doc mismatch, and two performance and boundary complaints. The agent rightly pushed back on the latter two with measurements. Round 1's single finding came from a later comment-trimming commit, 6963040, that removed the only citations of a canonical law token. The agent correctly kept the token because Canonical mirrors the law index. No round was caused by an incomplete fix.
guidance_observations: The agent answered three duplicate threads with one fix and identical replies on each, which kept the review state consistent at no extra cost.
The F2 pushback overstated its own case by claiming the stderr line only appears when a failure is being rendered; a pushback should concede the true sub-point even when it rejects the change.
